newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian state railway to hike tariffs again.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian state railway to hike tariffs again.

text.p: Bulgaria's debt-ridden state railway will raise tariffs by an average 20 percent this month to offset losses sparked by hikes in energy prices and a sharp fall in the lev, transport ministry officials said on Tuesday.
They said passenger fares would be increased from September 20 and freight fares would go up from October 1.
The lev fell to some 227 per dollar on Tuesday on the interbank market from 120 in May when tariffs were last raised.
Energy prices, updated every month, leapt by 118 percent in July and by an average 22 percent in August.
Railway officials said the passenger fares, quoted in dollars, were almost four times lower than they were six years ago due to the lev's depreciation.
The state railway company is on the government's list of 70 companies put on a special regime barring them from receiving bank credits under an austerity programme agreed with international lenders.

The railway, with a 2.7 billion lev loss in 1995, hopes to have a smaller loss this year but the government has not yet approved its proposals to close uneconomic secondary routes and to hive off three of its plants by making them independent firms.
